knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Kim_2024_islatravir"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Kim_2024_islatravir"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/psp4.13212> (open access, PMC11494919)
* Authors' code and digitised data: <https://github.com/KleistLab/ISL_PK-PD-PrEP>
  (GPL-3.0)
* Viral-dynamics source: Duwal S, Schuette C, von Kleist M. PLoS One
  2012;7(7):e40382, <https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0040382>

Kim et al. built an integrated model of islatravir (ISL) for HIV-1
pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP): plasma ISL after an oral tablet or a
subcutaneous (subdermal) implant, intracellular ISL-triphosphate (ISL-TP) in
peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMC), and the effect of ISL-TP on
reverse transcription inside an established HIV-1 viral dynamics model. The
model was fitted to published *mean* concentration-time profiles by least
squares, so it is a typical-value model: there is no between-subject
variability and no residual-error model.

# Population

The PK data are mean profiles digitised from five phase 1/2 studies
(Supplementary Table S1): ten oral plasma ISL and eleven oral PBMC ISL-TP
datasets after single doses of 0.5-400 mg (treatment-naive adults with HIV-1
for 0.5-30 mg; adults without HIV for 5-400 mg), and implant data for loading
doses of 48-62 mg in adults without HIV, with the implant removed at week 12
(plasma ISL and ISL-TP at 54 and 62 mg; ISL-TP only at 48, 52 and 56 mg).
About 83 of 114 individuals were male, mean age 45.4 years (18-60), mean BMI
26.1 kg/m2 (17.1-32). The antiviral potency IC50 was fitted to mean viral-load
declines after single oral doses of 0.5, 1, 2, 10 and 30 mg in 30
treatment-naive men with HIV-1 (6 per dose; Figure 2).

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Kim_2024_islatravir")()$population`.

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value carries an in-file comment naming its source. The
structure is Methods Equations (1)-(8) with Figure 1a.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|---|---|---|
| `d/dt(implant)`, `d/dt(sc)` | n/a | Eqs. (1)-(2); release clock = time since insertion |
| `d/dt(depot)` | n/a | Eq. (3) |
| `d/dt(central)` | n/a | Eq. (4) (equation image) |
| `d/dt(peripheral1)`, `d/dt(peripheral2)` | n/a | Eqs. (5)-(6) |
| `d/dt(pbmc_isltp)` | n/a | Eq. (7) |
| `eta_rt` (Emax inhibition) | n/a | Eq. (8) |
| viral-dynamics ODEs | n/a | deposit `code/steady_state.py`, `coupled_ode()`; Duwal 2012 |
| `phi_const` | n/a | Text S1 Eqs. (S1)-(S8); deposit `getExtinctionProbability()` |
| `lka` | log(0.4232) | Table 1 |
| `lksc_c`, `lksc_0` | log(0.0151), log(0.1521) | Table 1 |
| `lkel` | log(6.8999) | Table 1, kC->0 |
| `lk12`, `lk21` | log(1.8494), log(0.0023) | Table 1, kC->P1, kP1->C |
| `lk13`, `lk31` | log(5.2726), log(0.0237) | Table 1, kC->P2, kP2->C |
| `lvc` | fixed log(3.5) | Table 1 / Methods (physiological plasma volume) |
| `lkel_pbmc` | log(0.0088) | Table 1, kE->0 |
| `lkr` | log(2.18e-4) | Table S2 |
| `lkimpl_48` ... `lkimpl_62` | log(1.92e-4) ... log(4.60e-4) | Table S2 |
| `lfsc_le54`, `lfsc_gt54` | log(0.0412), log(0.0583) | Table S2, pi_ld |
| `lkce_oral_*` (10 doses) | 37.69 ... 9.10 | Table S2, kC->E (oral) |
| `lkce_oral_0p1`, `_0p25`, `_0p75` | 56.64, 40.32, 26.82 | Figure S6 legend |
| `lkce_implant_*` | 25.30 ... 36.87 | Table S2, kC->E (implant) |
| `kce_s6_int`, `kce_s6_exp` | 4.4, -0.371 | Figure S6 caption |
| `lic50` | log(429.707) | Results, "Pharmacodynamics" |
| viral-dynamics constants | see `ini()` | deposit `params_vd`; Duwal 2012 Table 2 |

## Units, and how to dose the model

Doses are in mg. Plasma ISL (`Cc`, the `central` state) is in nM, as in the
source. Intracellular ISL-TP is carried in nM (`pbmc_isltp`) and reported in
pmol per 10^6 cells as `Cpbmc_isltp`; the authors' code converts between the
two with a factor of 5555.6 nM per pmol/10^6 cells (0.18 pL per PBMC). The
viral-load output `d_viral_load` is the log10 change from baseline in total
plasma virus (infectious plus non-infectious), and `phi_const` is the
prophylactic efficacy that the current ISL-TP level would give if it were held
constant.

Every record carries two covariates: `ROUTE_ORAL` (1 = tablet, 0 = implant)
and `DOSE_ISLATRAVIR_MG` (the oral dose per administration, or the implant
load). Together they select the dose-specific parameters of Supplementary
Table S2.

* **Oral:** dose `amt = <mg>` into `depot`.
* **Implant insertion:** dose the full load **twice** at the same time, once
  into `implant` and once into `sc`. The model's `f()` gives `implant` the
  fraction `1 - pi` and `sc` the fraction `pi` (4.12% for loads of 54 mg or
  less, 5.83% above), reproducing the paper's initial condition.
* **Implant removal:** a replacement event (`evid = 5`, `amt = 0`) on
  `implant`, which stops release as in the source.

```{r helpers}
mod <- readModelDb("Kim_2024_islatravir")
mod_rx <- rxode2::rxode(mod)

oral_events <- function(dose, tau = 24, n = 1, obs) {
  et(amt = dose, cmt = "depot", ii = if (n > 1) tau else 0, addl = n - 1) |>
    et(obs) |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    mutate(DOSE_ISLATRAVIR_MG = dose, ROUTE_ORAL = 1L)
}

implant_events <- function(load, removal = 2016, obs) {
  et(amt = load, cmt = "implant") |>
    et(amt = load, cmt = "sc") |>
    et(time = removal, amt = 0, evid = 5, cmt = "implant") |>
    et(obs) |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    mutate(DOSE_ISLATRAVIR_MG = load, ROUTE_ORAL = 0L)
}

# Long dosing runs with no intermediate observations exhaust lsoda's default
# step budget, so every solve raises it.
solve_typical <- function(ev) {
  rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = ev, maxsteps = 1e6, returnType = "data.frame")
}
```

# Virtual cohort

The model has no random effects, so every simulation below is a single
typical subject per regimen: there is no cohort to draw. The covariates are
regimen descriptors (route and nominal dose), not subject characteristics.

# Observed data

The authors deposited their digitised mean profiles with the code. They are
embedded here (plasma ISL in nM, ISL-TP in pmol/10^6 cells, time in hours;
viral-load change in log10 copies/mL, time in days).

# Viral-dynamics baseline

The viral-dynamics states start at the untreated chronic-infection steady
state, which the model computes in closed form. The authors instead ran the
untreated system for 200 days from 10^11 uninfected T cells and 10 virions.
Both routes must land on the same equilibrium, and the closed-form start must
not drift.

```{r baseline}
ev_none <- et(seq(0, 200 * 24, by = 24)) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  mutate(DOSE_ISLATRAVIR_MG = 0, ROUTE_ORAL = 1L)
burn_in <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod,
  events = ev_none,
  inits = c(
    tcell_uninfected = 2e9 / 0.02, tcell_early = 0, tcell_infected = 0,
    virus = 10, macro_uninfected = 0, macro_early = 0, macro_infected = 0,
    virus_noninfectious = 0
  ),
  returnType = "data.frame"
)
held <- solve_typical(ev_none)

baseline <- tibble(
  State = c("Uninfected T cells", "Productively infected T cells",
            "Infectious virus", "Non-infectious virus"),
  `Closed form` = c(held$tu_ss[1], held$t2_ss[1], held$v_ss[1], held$vn_ss[1]),
  `200-day burn-in` = c(
    tail(burn_in$tcell_uninfected, 1), tail(burn_in$tcell_infected, 1),
    tail(burn_in$virus, 1), tail(burn_in$virus_noninfectious, 1)
  )
)
knitr::kable(baseline, digits = 0, format.args = list(big.mark = ","))

stopifnot(
  max(abs(baseline$`200-day burn-in` / baseline$`Closed form` - 1)) < 1e-4,
  max(abs(held$d_viral_load)) < 1e-5
)
```

# Replicate Figure 1: plasma ISL and PBMC ISL-TP

```{r fig1-sim}
pk_sim <- pk_obs |>
  distinct(type, dose) |>
  rowwise() |>
  do({
    row <- .
    obs_t <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 3000, by = 2), pk_obs$time[
      pk_obs$type == row$type & pk_obs$dose == row$dose
    ])))
    ev <- if (grepl("oral", row$type)) {
      oral_events(row$dose, obs = obs_t[obs_t <= 700])
    } else {
      implant_events(row$dose, obs = obs_t)
    }
    s <- solve_typical(ev)
    tibble(
      type = row$type, dose = row$dose, time = s$time,
      pred = if (grepl("intra", row$type)) s$Cpbmc_isltp else s$Cc
    )
  }) |>
  ungroup() |>
  distinct(type, dose, time, .keep_all = TRUE)
```

```{r fig1b, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 1b of Kim 2024: plasma ISL and PBMC ISL-TP after subcutaneous implants (removed at week 12, 2016 h). Points: digitised means from the authors' deposit; lines: packaged model."}
ggplot(filter(pk_sim, grepl("implant", type), pred > 0), aes(time, pred)) +
  geom_line(aes(colour = factor(dose))) +
  geom_point(
    data = filter(pk_obs, grepl("implant", type)),
    aes(time, obs, colour = factor(dose))
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~type, scales = "free_y", ncol = 1,
             labeller = as_labeller(c(implant_intra = "ISL-TP (pmol/10^6 cells)",
                                      implant_plasma = "Plasma ISL (nM)"))) +
  labs(x = "Time after insertion (h)", y = NULL, colour = "Load (mg)") +
  theme_bw()
```

```{r fig1c, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 6, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 1c of Kim 2024: plasma ISL (log scale) and PBMC ISL-TP after single oral doses. Points: digitised means; lines: packaged model."}
ggplot(filter(pk_sim, grepl("oral", type), pred > 0, time > 0), aes(time, pred)) +
  geom_line(aes(colour = factor(dose))) +
  geom_point(
    data = filter(pk_obs, grepl("oral", type)),
    aes(time, obs, colour = factor(dose))
  ) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  facet_wrap(~type, scales = "free_y", ncol = 1,
             labeller = as_labeller(c(oral_intra = "ISL-TP (pmol/10^6 cells)",
                                      oral_plasma = "Plasma ISL (nM)"))) +
  labs(x = "Time after dose (h)", y = NULL, colour = "Dose (mg)") +
  theme_bw()
```

```{r fig1-gate}
pk_fit <- pk_obs |>
  inner_join(pk_sim, by = c("type", "dose", "time")) |>
  mutate(log10_err = log10(pred / obs), pct = 100 * (pred - obs) / obs)
stopifnot(nrow(pk_fit) == nrow(pk_obs))

fit_tab <- pk_fit |>
  group_by(type) |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    median_abs_pct = median(abs(pct)),
    median_pct = median(pct),
    mean_abs_log10 = mean(abs(log10_err)),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
fit_tab |>
  rename(
    "Data set" = type, "Points" = n,
    "Median |% error|" = median_abs_pct, "Median % error" = median_pct,
    "Mean |log10 error|" = mean_abs_log10
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)

# A mis-transcribed rate constant or a wrong unit convention for the
# subcutaneous input moves these by tens of percent (the implant plasma set
# is the one that pins the sc unit convention). Measured medians: 9-19%,
# biases within 6%.
stopifnot(
  all(fit_tab$median_abs_pct < 25),
  all(abs(fit_tab$median_pct) < 10)
)
```

The paper reports average percentage deviations of 11.7% (oral plasma), 2.56%
(oral ISL-TP), 12.87% (implant plasma) and 3.8% (implant ISL-TP). The authors
fitted the oral data and the ISL-TP data after log10 transformation, and the
smaller intracellular figures appear to be computed on that scale; the
packaged model's median absolute errors on the linear scale are in the table
above and the agreement is visible in the two figures.

```{r fig2-gate}
vl_fit <- vl_obs |>
  mutate(pred = mapply(function(d, t) {
    v <- vl_sim$pred[vl_sim$dose == d & abs(vl_sim$time_day - t) < 1e-9]
    if (length(v) != 1L) stop("no unique prediction for ", d, " mg at day ", t)

# Prophylactic efficacy thresholds (Figure S4)

Holding the intracellular ISL-TP concentration constant, the paper derives the
levels giving 85% and 90% reduction in infection risk per exposure:
EC85 = 0.35 and EC90 = 0.51 pmol/10^6 cells. `phi_const` reproduces them.

```{r ec-thresholds}
phi_at <- function(pmol) {
  ev <- et(0) |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    mutate(DOSE_ISLATRAVIR_MG = 0, ROUTE_ORAL = 1L)
  rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = ev, inits = c(pbmc_isltp = pmol * 5555.6),
                  returnType = "data.frame")$phi_const[1]
}
ec <- vapply(c(0.85, 0.90), function(p) {
  uniroot(function(x) phi_at(x) - p, c(0.01, 5), tol = 1e-8)$root
}, numeric(1))
ec_tab <- tibble(
  Threshold = c("EC85", "EC90"),
  `Paper (pmol/10^6 cells)` = c(0.35, 0.51),
  `Model (pmol/10^6 cells)` = ec
)
knitr::kable(ec_tab, digits = 3)
# Measured 0.353 and 0.511; the paper rounds to two decimals.
stopifnot(abs(ec / c(0.35, 0.51) - 1) < 0.02)
```

# Dose-specific uptake for untested oral doses (Figure S6)

For oral doses that were not in the fitted data, the paper reads kC->E off the
power law kC->E = x^-0.371 e^4.4, where x is the steady-state plasma maximum of
the same dose given once weekly. The model carries the per-mg weekly
steady-state maximum (26.62 nM/mg); this check confirms that the packaged
plasma model gives that value, and that the power law reproduces the three
extrapolated values the paper lists in the Figure S6 legend.

```{r fig-s6}
wk <- solve_typical(oral_events(1, tau = 168, n = 60,
                                obs = seq(59 * 168, 60 * 168, by = 0.02)))
cmax_wk_per_mg <- max(wk$Cc)

kce_power <- function(dose) exp(4.4) * (26.62 * dose)^-0.371
s6 <- tibble(
  `Dose (mg)` = c(0.1, 0.25, 0.75),
  `Figure S6 legend` = c(56.64, 40.32, 26.82),
  `Power law` = kce_power(c(0.1, 0.25, 0.75)),
  `Model kce` = vapply(c(0.1, 0.25, 0.75), function(d) {
    solve_typical(oral_events(d, obs = 1))$kce[1]
  }, numeric(1))
)
knitr::kable(s6, digits = 2)
cat("Weekly steady-state Cmax per mg:", signif(cmax_wk_per_mg, 5), "nM\n")

stopifnot(
  abs(cmax_wk_per_mg / 26.62 - 1) < 0.005,
  all(abs(s6$`Power law` / s6$`Figure S6 legend` - 1) < 0.005),
  # an oral dose outside the table takes the power law
  abs(solve_typical(oral_events(3, obs = 1))$kce[1] / kce_power(3) - 1) < 1e-8
)
```

# Replicate Table 2: toxicity threshold and time above it

The paper takes the plasma maximum after 0.25 mg once daily as the
no-observed-adverse-effect level (NOAEL, 7.02 nM) and reports, for each
regimen at steady state, the fraction of time plasma ISL exceeds it and a
plasma AUC expressed per 24 h.

```{r table2}
regimen <- function(dose, tau, n) {
  s <- solve_typical(oral_events(dose, tau = tau, n = n,
                                 obs = seq((n - 1) * tau, n * tau, by = 0.02)))
  w <- filter(s, time >= (n - 1) * tau, time < n * tau)
  tibble(
    cmax = max(w$Cc),
    time_above = 100 * mean(w$Cc > 7.02),
    auc_per_24h = sum(diff(s$time) * (head(s$Cc, -1) + tail(s$Cc, -1)) / 2) /
      (tau / 24)
  )
}
# One year of dosing reaches steady state for the slow peripheral I phase
# (kP1->C = 0.0023 1/h, half-life about 300 h).
tab2 <- tribble(
  ~dose, ~regimen, ~tau, ~paper_auc, ~paper_above,
  0.1, "once daily", 24, 12.99, 0.0,
  0.25, "once daily", 24, 32.49, 0.0,
  0.5, "once daily", 24, 64.97, 9.5,
  0.75, "once daily", 24, 97.46, 14.9,
  2, "once weekly", 168, 36.89, 3.4,
  5, "once weekly", 168, 92.21, 5.4,
  10, "once weekly", 168, 184.44, 9.7,
  10, "once biweekly", 336, 92.73, 4.0,
  15, "once biweekly", 336, 139.1, 8.9,
  30, "once monthly", 672, 138.65, 10.8,
  60, "once monthly", 672, 277.29, 19.4
) |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(sim = list(regimen(dose, tau, ceiling(365 * 24 / tau)))) |>
  ungroup() |>
  unnest(sim) |>
  mutate(auc_ratio = auc_per_24h / paper_auc)

tab2 |>
  select(dose, regimen, paper_auc, auc_per_24h, auc_ratio, paper_above, time_above) |>
  rename(
    "Dose (mg)" = dose, "Regimen" = regimen,
    "AUC per 24 h, paper (nM h)" = paper_auc,
    "AUC per 24 h, model (nM h)" = auc_per_24h,
    "Model / paper" = auc_ratio,
    "Time above NOAEL, paper (%)" = paper_above,
    "Time above NOAEL, model (%)" = time_above
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)

noael <- tab2$cmax[tab2$dose == 0.25 & tab2$regimen == "once daily"]
cat("Steady-state Cmax for 0.25 mg once daily:", round(noael, 2),
    "nM (paper NOAEL 7.02 nM)\n")

low <- tab2$paper_above < 6
stopifnot(
  abs(noael / 7.02 - 1) < 0.06,
  # Regimens the paper rates safe or near-safe (< 6% of time above the
  # NOAEL): within 1.5 percentage points (measured 0.0-1.1).
  all(abs(tab2$time_above - tab2$paper_above)[low] < 1.5),
  # Higher-exposure regimens: a known deviation, see below. The model sits
  # above the paper by 4-29% relative (measured); the bound still fails if
  # the plasma peak moves by a few tens of percent.
  all((tab2$time_above / tab2$paper_above)[!low] > 1),
  all((tab2$time_above / tab2$paper_above)[!low] < 1.35),
  # The AUC column sits a constant 8% below the model for every oral regimen
  # (measured ratios 1.086-1.092), so the offset is definitional, not a PK
  # discrepancy; a wrong clearance would move the ratio for every row.
  all(abs(tab2$auc_ratio - 1.09) < 0.02)
)
```

```{r table2-implant}
implant_tab <- tribble(
  ~load, ~paper_auc, ~paper_above,
  48, 6.51, 0.0,
  52, 9.2, 0.0,
  54, 10.27, 0.1,
  56, 11.83, 0.2,
  62, 15.71, 0.2
) |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(sim = list({
    s <- solve_typical(implant_events(load, obs = seq(0, 2016, by = 0.02))) |>
      filter(time <= 2016) |>
      distinct(time, .keep_all = TRUE)
    tibble(
      auc_per_24h = sum(diff(s$time) * (head(s$Cc, -1) + tail(s$Cc, -1)) / 2) / 84,
      time_above = 100 * mean(s$Cc > 7.02)
    )
  })) |>
  ungroup() |>
  unnest(sim) |>
  mutate(auc_ratio = auc_per_24h / paper_auc)

implant_tab |>
  rename(
    "Load (mg)" = load, "AUC per 24 h, paper (nM h)" = paper_auc,
    "Time above NOAEL, paper (%)" = paper_above,
    "AUC per 24 h, model (nM h)" = auc_per_24h,
    "Time above NOAEL, model (%)" = time_above, "Model / paper" = auc_ratio
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)

stopifnot(
  all(abs(implant_tab$time_above - implant_tab$paper_above) < 0.15),
  # Constant ratio across loads again (measured 1.108-1.110).
  max(implant_tab$auc_ratio) - min(implant_tab$auc_ratio) < 0.01
)
```

The model evaluates every regimen after one year of dosing, when the slow
peripheral I phase has reached steady state. The paper does not state the
dosing duration it evaluated, and its numbers are not all from one: the
0.25 mg once-daily plasma maximum reaches its NOAEL of 7.02 nM after about one
week of dosing in this model and 7.29 nM at full steady state, while its
AUC column matches about 25 days. The regimens the paper rates safe or nearly
safe are reproduced within about one percentage point of time above the NOAEL.
The higher-exposure regimens (10 mg weekly, 15 mg biweekly, 30 and 60 mg
monthly) come out 21-29% higher in relative terms (for example 12.6% against
9.7% for 10 mg weekly), which is consistent with the paper evaluating them
before steady state. Two of them move up one band of the paper's colour
scale, from 5-10% to 10-15% (10 mg weekly and 15 mg biweekly); the monthly
regimens stay in their bands. The AUC column of Table 2 is "plasma
AUC for tau = 24 h"; the model's AUC over one dosing interval, scaled to 24 h,
is a constant 9% (oral) or 11% (implant, over the 12-week insertion) above it
for every regimen, which points to a different evaluation window or
normalisation rather than a different exposure.

```{r fig3, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5, fig.cap = "Replicates the once-daily panel of Kim 2024 Figure 3: plasma ISL (top) and PBMC ISL-TP (bottom) for 0.1, 0.25 and 0.5 mg once daily, with the NOAEL and the EC85 / EC90 thresholds."}

  s <- solve_typical(oral_events(d, tau = 24, n = 30, obs = seq(0, 30 * 24, by = 0.5)))
  tibble(dose = d, time_day = s$time / 24, Cc = s$Cc, Cpbmc = s$Cpbmc_isltp)
}) |>
  bind_rows() |>
  pivot_longer(c(Cc, Cpbmc), names_to = "matrix", values_to = "conc")
thresholds <- tibble(
  matrix = c("Cc", "Cpbmc", "Cpbmc"),
  conc = c(7.02, 0.35, 0.51),
  label = c("NOAEL", "EC85", "EC90")
)
ggplot(fig3, aes(time_day, conc, colour = factor(dose))) +

trough <- fig3 |>
  filter(matrix == "Cpbmc", abs(time_day - 29) < 1e-9)
# Results: 0.1 mg once daily gives > 90% protection from day 12 on, so its

# Implant protection after insertion (Figure 4b, constant-exposure view)

Figure 4b shows the time-resolved prophylactic efficacy, which the authors
compute by solving the extinction-probability equations of Text S1 backwards
in time from each exposure. That backward solve has no forward-in-time ODE
form and is not part of the packaged model. `phi_const`, the efficacy the
current ISL-TP level would give if held constant, is shown instead. It is not
the same quantity: it ignores the protection carried forward by ISL-TP that
persists after an exposure, and it drifts down during wear as the release
rate decays (for 62 mg from 0.94 in the first week to 0.83 by week 12). It
does reproduce the paper's ranking of the loads: only 56 and 62 mg ever reach
90%, and 52 mg sits above 54 mg because its fitted ISL-TP uptake is higher
(the paper's Discussion notes the same inversion in the data).

```{r fig4b, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4, fig.cap = "Constant-exposure prophylactic efficacy (phi_const) during 12 weeks of implant wear, by load. Dashed and dotted lines: 85% and 90%."}
fig4 <- lapply(c(48, 52, 54, 56, 62), function(ld) {
  s <- solve_typical(implant_events(ld, obs = seq(0, 2400, by = 4)))
  tibble(load = ld, time_day = s$time / 24, phi = s$phi_const)
}) |>
  bind_rows() |>
  distinct(load, time_day, .keep_all = TRUE)
ggplot(fig4, aes(time_day, 100 * phi, colour = factor(load))) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(85, 90), linetype = c("dashed", "dotted")) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 84, colour = "red") +
  labs(x = "Time after insertion (days)", y = "Prophylactic efficacy (%)",
       colour = "Load (mg)") +
  theme_bw()

wear <- fig4 |>
  filter(time_day <= 84) |>
  group_by(load) |>
  summarise(max_phi = max(phi), median_phi = median(phi), .groups = "drop") |>
  arrange(load)
knitr::kable(
  rename(wear, "Load (mg)" = load, "Maximum phi_const" = max_phi,
         "Median phi_const" = median_phi),
  digits = 3
)
# Measured maxima 0.756 / 0.851 / 0.779 / 0.925 / 0.938 for 48-62 mg.
stopifnot(
  all(wear$max_phi[wear$load >= 56] > 0.90),
  all(wear$max_phi[wear$load <= 54] < 0.88),
  identical(wear$load[order(wear$median_phi)], c(48, 54, 52, 56, 62))
)
```

# PKNCA: single oral doses

The paper does not tabulate NCA, but it states that ISL-TP had an
intracellular half-life of 87.75 h in the model, in line with the 78.5-128 h
reported clinically for 0.5-30 mg. PKNCA on the packaged model's single-dose
profiles gives the apparent terminal half-life of PBMC ISL-TP; the comparison
with 87.75 h is discussed under "Assumptions and deviations".

```{r pknca}
nca_doses <- c(0.5, 2, 10, 30)
nca_sim <- lapply(nca_doses, function(d) {
  s <- solve_typical(oral_events(d, obs = c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 6,
                                            8, 12, 24, 48, 72, 96, 120, 144,
                                            168, 240, 336)))
  tibble(id = 1L, treatment = paste(d, "mg"), dose = d, time = s$time,
         Cc = s$Cc, Cpbmc = s$Cpbmc_isltp)
}) |>
  bind_rows() |>
  distinct(treatment, time, .keep_all = TRUE)

dose_df <- nca_sim |>
  distinct(id, treatment, dose) |>
  mutate(time = 0)

nca_one <- function(col) {
  conc <- nca_sim |>
    rename(conc = all_of(col)) |>
    filter(!is.na(conc))
  o_conc <- PKNCAconc(conc, conc ~ time | treatment + id)
  o_dose <- PKNCAdose(dose_df, dose ~ time | treatment + id)
  intervals <- data.frame(
    start = 0, end = Inf, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE,
    aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE
  )
  as.data.frame(pk.nca(PKNCAdata(o_conc, o_dose, intervals = intervals)))
}
nca_cc <- nca_one("Cc")
nca_pbmc <- nca_one("Cpbmc")

nca_pbmc |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "tmax", "half.life")) |>
  select(treatment, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES) |>
  rename("Dose" = treatment, "ISL-TP Cmax (pmol/10^6 cells)" = cmax,
         "Tmax (h)" = tmax, "Terminal t1/2 (h)" = half.life) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)
```

```{r nca-compare}
sim_hl <- nca_pbmc |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "half.life") |>
  select(treatment, PPTESTCD, PPORRES)
ref_hl <- tibble(treatment = unique(sim_hl$treatment), half.life = 87.75)
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = sim_hl,
  reference = ref_hl,
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(half.life = "h")
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = paste(
  "ISL-TP apparent terminal half-life from PKNCA (0-336 h) against the",
  "87.75 h the paper reports for its model (Discussion). * marks a",
  "difference above 20%."
))
# The apparent half-life is longer than the intrinsic log(2)/kE->0 = 78.8 h
# because plasma ISL, fed back from the peripheral I reservoir (Figure S3),
# keeps supplying the PBMC compartment. It must fall inside the 78.5-128 h
# the paper cites from the clinical 0.5-30 mg data (measured 112.9 h), and
# it is dose-independent because the PK is linear in time.
stopifnot(
  all(sim_hl$PPORRES > 78.5 & sim_hl$PPORRES < 128),
  diff(range(sim_hl$PPORRES)) < 0.01
)

# Plasma ISL is linear: dose-normalised Cmax is the same at every dose.
cmax_cc <- nca_cc |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "cmax") |>
  left_join(distinct(nca_sim, treatment, dose), by = "treatment")
stopifnot(diff(range(cmax_cc$PPORRES / cmax_cc$dose)) /
            mean(cmax_cc$PPORRES / cmax_cc$dose) < 1e-3)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Code deposit as a source.** The paper prints the structure (Eqs. 1-8,
  Text S1) and the fitted PK, implant and IC50 values, but not the units of
  each state, the PBMC unit conversion, or the viral-dynamics constants. These
  come from the authors' deposited code (GPL-3.0), which generated the
  paper's figures; every value taken from it is marked "deposit" in the model
  file.
* **Viral-dynamics constants differ from Duwal 2012 in three places.** The
  deposit, which produced Figure 2 and the IC50 fit, uses deltaT1 = 0.5/day,
  deltaT2 = 1.4/day and betaM = 1e-13, whereas Duwal 2012 Table 2 lists
  deltaT = deltaT1 = 0.02/day, deltaT2 = 1/day and betaM = 1e-14. The deposit
  values are kept, because IC50 = 429.707 nM was fitted with them; with the
  Duwal 2012 values the fitted IC50 would not apply.
* **Subcutaneous input on the published scale.** Eq. 4 adds kSC->C x SC to the
  plasma *concentration* without dividing by VC, and the deposit holds SC in
  nmol. The model keeps that form, so kSC->C and the implant data fit belong
  together; the implant plasma data are reproduced within 10% (median).
* **Implant clock.** Eq. 1 uses time since the start of the simulation, with
  the implant always inserted at time 0. The model uses time since the
  implant dose (`tad(implant)`), which is identical for the paper's scenarios
  and also supports a later or repeated insertion.
* **Implant loads outside the five studied ones** return NA for kC->E and the
  release rate; the paper gives no rule for them (its 48, 52 and 56 mg release
  rates were interpolated from in vitro release data, not from a formula).
* **Untested oral doses** use the Figure S6 power law, as the paper did for
  0.1, 0.25 and 0.75 mg (whose legend values are also carried as table
  entries). The paper's "plasma concentration at steady state" for that law is
  identified here as the weekly steady-state maximum: it is the only summary
  for which all three legend values back-solve to the same per-mg
  concentration (26.62 nM/mg), and the packaged plasma model gives 26.618.
* **ISL-TP half-life of 87.75 h.** The Discussion gives this as the model's
  intracellular half-life, but Table 1's kE->0 = 0.0088 1/h corresponds to
  log(2)/0.0088 = 78.8 h. 87.75 h is log(2)/0.0079, and 0.0079 is the starting
  value of kE->0 in the deposit's fitting script, so the Discussion figure
  appears to come from an earlier fit. The model uses the Table 1 estimate.
  The apparent terminal half-life of the simulated ISL-TP profile (113 h over
  two weeks) is longer than either, because plasma ISL returning from the
  slow peripheral compartment keeps feeding the PBMC compartment.
* **Time-resolved prophylactic efficacy** (Eq. 9, Figure 4) needs a backward
  solve of the extinction-probability equations for each exposure time and is
  not packaged. `phi_const` packages the constant-exposure efficacy that
  defines EC85 and EC90.
* **Clearance of free virus.** The viral-load fit uses CL = 23/day (chronic
  infection) and the prophylactic efficacy uses 2.3/day (at exposure), as in
  the deposit and Duwal 2012 Table 2.
* **No IIV or residual error.** The model was fitted to mean profiles by
  least squares; the paper reports bootstrap standard deviations of the
  parameters, not between-subject variability.
